questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The minister's speech was so VERBOSE that the audience grew restless."
questions.explanation: Verbose means using more words than needed, i.e. wordy. 'Brief' is its antonym.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The judge remained IMPARTIAL throughout the trial."
questions.explanation: Impartial = not favouring either side = unbiased. 'Prejudiced' is the opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "His FRUGAL habits helped him save for his daughter's education."
questions.explanation: Frugal means careful and economical with money = thrifty. 'Extravagant' is the antonym.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The old fort now stands in a DILAPIDATED condition."
questions.explanation: Dilapidated describes a building fallen into disrepair, i.e. run-down or ruined.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The headmaster tried to PLACATE the angry parents."
questions.explanation: Placate = to calm someone down and make them less angry = pacify. 'Provoke' is the opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "Her CANDID reply surprised the interview board."
questions.explanation: Candid means truthful and straightforward = frank. 'Evasive' is the opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The child's INCESSANT chatter disturbed the whole class."
questions.explanation: Incessant = continuing without a pause = unceasing. 'Occasional' is the opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The fishermen were APPREHENSIVE about the approaching cyclone."
questions.explanation: Apprehensive means worried that something bad will happen = anxious.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The teacher gave a LUCID explanation of the theorem."
questions.explanation: Lucid = expressed clearly and easy to understand. 'Confusing' is the opposite.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The thief made a FUTILE attempt to escape from the police."
questions.explanation: Futile means producing no useful result = useless/vain.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "Her DILIGENT research finally led to a breakthrough."
questions.explanation: Diligent = showing steady, careful effort = hard-working (industrious).

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The tyrant's RUTHLESS orders terrified the people."
questions.explanation: Ruthless = without pity or compassion = merciless.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The manuscript was written in an OBSCURE dialect that few scholars knew."
questions.explanation: Obscure here means not well known; the clause 'that few scholars knew' confirms it.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The general's AUDACIOUS plan took the enemy by surprise."
questions.explanation: Audacious = showing a willingness to take bold risks = daring. 'Timid' and 'cautious' are opposites.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The workers were offered a PALTRY sum as a bonus."
questions.explanation: Paltry = very small or insignificant in amount = meagre.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The professor's ERUDITE lecture impressed even the senior scholars."
questions.explanation: Erudite means having or showing great knowledge = learned/scholarly.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "His SYCOPHANTIC behaviour towards the manager annoyed his colleagues."
questions.explanation: A sycophant flatters powerful people to gain advantage; sycophantic = fawning, servilely flattering.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The villagers faced the long drought with remarkable FORTITUDE."
questions.explanation: Fortitude = courage and strength in bearing pain or hardship = endurance.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The victim's statement was CORROBORATED by two independent witnesses."
questions.explanation: To corroborate is to confirm or support a statement with further evidence.

questions.prompt: Choose the synonym of the word in capitals: "The scholar's argument was so COGENT that nobody could refute it."
questions.explanation: Cogent = clear, logical and convincing. 'Nobody could refute it' supports this.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The climate of the hill station is SALUBRIOUS."
questions.explanation: Salubrious means health-giving; its opposite is unhealthy (insalubrious).

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The village has an ANCIENT temple on the river bank."
questions.explanation: Ancient = very old; its opposite is modern.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The workers were RELUCTANT to accept the new shift system."
questions.explanation: Reluctant = unwilling; the opposite is willing (eager).

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The speaker's remarks were RELEVANT to the topic."
questions.explanation: Relevant = connected with the matter; the opposite is irrelevant (formed with the prefix ir-).

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "Kamarajar was admired for his HUMILITY."
questions.explanation: Humility = modesty, lack of pride; its opposite is arrogance. 'Modesty' is a synonym.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "After the storm the boat was in a PRECARIOUS position."
questions.explanation: Precarious = dangerously unstable; the opposite is secure (safe). The other three are near-synonyms.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The new law was passed to PROHIBIT child labour."
questions.explanation: Prohibit = forbid; its opposite is permit (allow). 'Forbid' and 'ban' are synonyms.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "Veerapandiya Kattabomman is remembered for his VALOUR."
questions.explanation: Valour = great courage; the opposite is cowardice.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The SCARCITY of water forced many families to migrate."
questions.explanation: Scarcity = shortage; its opposite is abundance (plenty). 'Dearth' and 'lack' are synonyms.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The new warden is very LENIENT with latecomers."
questions.explanation: Lenient = merciful, not strict; its opposite is strict (severe).

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "She has taken up a TEMPORARY job during the vacation."
questions.explanation: Temporary = lasting for a limited time; its opposite is permanent.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The rich merchant was known for his PARSIMONIOUS nature."
questions.explanation: Parsimonious = extremely unwilling to spend money (stingy, miserly). Its opposite is generous.

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The witness gave only a VAGUE account of the accident."
questions.explanation: Vague = not clear or definite; its opposite is precise (exact).

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The committee's decision was UNANIMOUS."
questions.explanation: Unanimous = agreed by everyone; its opposite is divided (split).

questions.prompt: Choose the antonym of the word in capitals: "The student's conduct during the camp was EXEMPLARY."
questions.explanation: Exemplary = serving as a fine example; its opposite is deplorable (shockingly bad). The other three are synonyms.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a place to live or stay'.
questions.explanation: Accommodation has double 'c' and double 'm'.
questions.trick: Two Cs and two Ms: aCCoMModation.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'needed; essential'.
questions.explanation: Necessary: one 'c', double 's'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'to make someone feel awkward or ashamed'.
questions.explanation: Embarrass has double 'r' and double 's'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a period of a thousand years'.
questions.explanation: Millennium has double 'l' and double 'n' (from Latin mille + annus).

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'careful to do one's work well and thoroughly'.
questions.explanation: Conscientious = science + -tious: c-o-n-s-c-i-e-n-t-i-o-u-s.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a regular, repeated pattern of sound or movement'.
questions.explanation: Rhythm: r-h-y-t-h-m, with 'h' after both 'r' and 't' and no vowel before 'm'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'to divide or keep apart'.
questions.explanation: Separate has 'a' after the 'p': sep-A-rate.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'an incident or event that happens'.
questions.explanation: Occurrence: double 'c', double 'r', and ends in -ence.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following words is INCORRECTLY spelt?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling is 'definitely' (from 'finite'). The other three are correctly spelt.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a system of government run by appointed officials'.
questions.explanation: Bureaucracy = bureau + -cracy: b-u-r-e-a-u-c-r-a-c-y.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a printed set of questions used in a survey'.
questions.explanation: Questionnaire has double 'n' and ends in -aire.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a person who sets up a business, taking financial risk'.
questions.explanation: Entrepreneur: entre-pre-neur (French origin).

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'communication or co-operation between groups'.
questions.explanation: Liaison: l-i-a-i-s-o-n, with 'i' on both sides of the 'a'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'the work of keeping something in good condition'.
questions.explanation: Although the verb is 'maintain', the noun is spelt 'maintenance'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly spelt word that means 'a special right or advantage given to a person or group'.
questions.explanation: Privilege has no 'd': p-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a person who travels on foot along a road':
questions.explanation: A pedestrian is a person walking rather than travelling in a vehicle.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a substance applied to wounds to prevent infection by killing germs':
questions.explanation: An antiseptic prevents the growth of germs. An anaesthetic removes pain, an antidote counters poison, a sedative calms.

questions.prompt: One word for 'the killing of a king':
questions.explanation: Regicide (Latin rex/regis = king). Patricide = killing one's father; genocide = killing of a whole people.

questions.prompt: One word for 'animals that feed only on plants':
questions.explanation: Herbivorous animals eat plants. Carnivores eat flesh; omnivores eat both.

questions.prompt: One word for 'government of the people, by the people, for the people':
questions.explanation: Lincoln's famous definition describes democracy (demos = people).

questions.prompt: One word for 'government by a small group of powerful people':
questions.explanation: Oligarchy (Greek oligoi = few). Anarchy = absence of government.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a list of the books and articles referred to in a piece of research':
questions.explanation: A bibliography lists sources used. A glossary explains difficult words; a biography is a life story.

questions.prompt: One word for 'the story of a person's life written by that person himself or herself':
questions.explanation: Autobiography = auto (self) + biography. A biography is written by someone else.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a speech delivered without previous preparation':
questions.explanation: Extempore means spoken or done without preparation.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a person whose bad habits cannot be corrected':
questions.explanation: Incorrigible = not able to be corrected or reformed.

questions.prompt: One word for 'one who cannot be conquered or defeated':
questions.explanation: Invincible = too strong to be defeated. Indelible = cannot be erased; inaudible = cannot be heard.

questions.prompt: One word for 'an abnormal fear of heights':
questions.explanation: Acro- = height. Hydrophobia = fear of water; agoraphobia = fear of open/public places; claustrophobia = fear of closed spaces.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a person who is new to a job or activity and has little experience':
questions.explanation: A novice is a beginner. A veteran has long experience.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a person with expert knowledge and fine taste in matters such as art, music or food':
questions.explanation: A connoisseur is an expert judge in matters of taste. A glutton simply eats too much.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a place where bees are kept':
questions.explanation: Apiary (Latin apis = bee). An aviary is for birds; a granary stores grain.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a large cage or enclosure in which birds are kept':
questions.explanation: Aviary (Latin avis = bird). A kennel is for dogs; a stable for horses.

questions.prompt: One word for 'words inscribed on a tomb in memory of the person buried there':
questions.explanation: An epitaph is a tomb inscription. An epigram is a witty saying; an epithet is a descriptive name.

questions.prompt: One word for 'that which cannot be avoided':
questions.explanation: Inevitable = certain to happen; unavoidable.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a child born after the death of its father':
questions.explanation: Posthumous means occurring after death; a posthumous child is born after the father has died.

questions.prompt: One word for 'a doctor who specialises in the treatment of children':
questions.explanation: Paediatrician (Greek pais = child). A dermatologist treats skin diseases.

questions.prompt: One word for 'the scientific study of insects':
questions.explanation: Entomology studies insects. Ornithology = birds; ichthyology = fish; anthropology = human societies.

questions.prompt: One word for 'the scientific study of birds':
questions.explanation: Ornithology (Greek ornis = bird). Herpetology = reptiles.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The examiners will judge the essays on three ___." (criterion)
questions.explanation: Criterion (Greek) takes the plural 'criteria'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "An eclipse is one of the most striking natural ___." (phenomenon)
questions.explanation: Phenomenon (Greek) takes the plural 'phenomena'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The country faced several economic ___ in that decade." (crisis)
questions.explanation: Nouns ending in -is change to -es: crisis -> crises, basis -> bases.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The laboratory carried out two separate ___ of the water sample." (analysis)
questions.explanation: Analysis -> analyses (-is becomes -es).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "Both his ___ attended the wedding." (son-in-law)
questions.explanation: In compound nouns the main word takes the plural: sons-in-law.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "A few ___ stopped to help the injured man." (passer-by)
questions.explanation: The main noun 'passer' takes the plural: passers-by.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "Keep the ___ out of the reach of children." (knife)
questions.explanation: Knife -> knives (f changes to v + es), like wife -> wives.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "She bought two kilograms of ___ from the market." (potato)
questions.explanation: Potato and tomato add -es: potatoes, tomatoes.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The farmer yoked two ___ to the plough." (ox)
questions.explanation: Ox has the irregular plural 'oxen'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The children were treated for head ___." (louse)
questions.explanation: Louse -> lice, like mouse -> mice (vowel change).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The two tribal ___ signed the peace treaty." (chief)
questions.explanation: Chief is an exception to the f -> ves rule: chiefs (also roofs, beliefs).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "The meeting was attended by the ___ of the three armed forces." (commander-in-chief)
questions.explanation: The principal noun 'commander' is pluralised: commanders-in-chief.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct plural: "Many ___ of the college attended its centenary celebration." (alumnus)
questions.explanation: Alumnus (Latin) -> alumni. (The feminine alumna -> alumnae.)

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Mathematics ___ my favourite subject."
questions.explanation: Nouns like mathematics, physics and economics look plural but take a singular verb when naming a subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "The cattle ___ grazing in the field."
questions.explanation: 'Cattle' is always plural in form and use, so it takes a plural verb.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He gave me some useful informations.
He gave me an useful information.
He gave me some useful information.
He gave me a useful informations.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable: no plural form and no article 'a/an'.

questions.prompt: Which of these nouns is used ONLY in the plural and takes a plural verb?
questions.explanation: Trousers (like scissors, spectacles) are plural nouns. Furniture, luggage and machinery are uncountable and take singular verbs.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'Bring some fruits, e.g. mangoes and bananas', the abbreviation 'e.g.' stands for:
questions.explanation: e.g. = exempli gratia, Latin for 'for the sake of example'. 'i.e.' = id est.

questions.prompt: In 'pens, pencils, erasers, etc.', the abbreviation 'etc.' stands for:
questions.explanation: etc. = et cetera, Latin for 'and the rest / and so on'.

questions.prompt: In '9 a.m.', the abbreviation 'a.m.' stands for:
questions.explanation: a.m. = ante meridiem (before noon); p.m. = post meridiem (after noon).

questions.prompt: The abbreviation 'viz.' (as in 'three colours, viz. red, white and green') means:
questions.explanation: viz. is short for Latin videlicet, meaning 'namely'.

questions.prompt: In police procedure, 'FIR' stands for:
questions.explanation: An FIR (First Information Report) is the written document prepared by the police when they receive information about a cognisable offence.

questions.prompt: In 'PIN code', 'PIN' stands for:
questions.explanation: India Post's six-digit PIN = Postal Index Number. (In banking, PIN = Personal Identification Number, but not in a postal address.)

questions.prompt: The abbreviation 'A.D.' used with dates stands for:
questions.explanation: A.D. = Anno Domini, Latin for 'in the year of the Lord'.

questions.prompt: In footnotes, 'ibid.' means:
options: in the same place (as the previous reference)
questions.explanation: ibid. is short for Latin ibidem, 'in the same place', used when citing the same source again.

questions.prompt: 'UNESCO' stands for:
options: United Nations Economic, Social and Cultural Organization
United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization
United Nations Educational, Social and Children's Organization
Universal Network for Education, Science and Culture
questions.explanation: UNESCO = United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (headquarters in Paris).

questions.prompt: In 'India vs. Australia', the abbreviation 'vs.' stands for:
questions.explanation: vs. = versus (Latin 'against').

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The ___ of the mountain was covered with snow."
questions.explanation: Peak = the pointed top of a mountain. Peek = a quick look; pique = resentment.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The bride walked slowly down the ___ of the church."
questions.explanation: Aisle = a passage between rows of seats. Isle = a small island; ail = to trouble or be ill.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The two armies agreed to ___ fire at midnight."
questions.explanation: Cease = stop. Seize = take hold of by force.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Customs officers managed to ___ the smuggled gold at the airport."
questions.explanation: Seize = take possession of by force or legal authority. Cease = stop.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The boy ___ the ball over the wall."
questions.explanation: Threw is the past tense of throw. Through = from one side to the other.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Turn ___ at the next signal to reach the bus stand."
questions.explanation: Right = the direction opposite to left. Write = put words on paper; rite = a ceremony.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Gunny bags are made of ___ jute fibre."
questions.explanation: Coarse = rough in texture. Course = a route or a series of lessons.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The city ___ met to discuss the drinking-water problem."
questions.explanation: Council = an elected or appointed body. Counsel = advice, or a lawyer; consul = a diplomatic official.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The tiger crouched silently, waiting for its ___."
questions.explanation: Prey = an animal hunted for food. Pray = speak to God.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Dark clouds gathered and heavy rain seemed ___."
questions.explanation: Imminent = about to happen. Eminent = famous and respected; immanent = existing within.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Dr. S. Radhakrishnan was an ___ philosopher and teacher."
questions.explanation: Eminent = famous and respected within a field. Imminent = about to happen.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The elderly passenger asked for a lower ___ in the sleeper coach."
questions.explanation: Berth = a sleeping place on a train or ship. Birth = being born.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Press the ___ gently when the car goes downhill."
questions.explanation: Brakes = the device used to slow a vehicle. Breaks = pauses, or the verb 'to break'.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "These slippers are too ___ for me; they keep falling off."
questions.explanation: Loose = not tight. Lose = fail to keep or to win.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Everyone went on the trip ___ Ravi, who was ill."
questions.explanation: Except = not including. Accept = receive willingly.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "The miser kept a secret ___ of gold coins under the floor."
questions.explanation: Hoard = a hidden store of valuables. Horde = a large crowd.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "A ___ of tourists rushed into the museum when the doors opened."
questions.explanation: Horde = a large, often noisy crowd. Hoard = a hidden store.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct word: "Students must ___ their sources at the end of the project report."
questions.explanation: Cite = quote or mention as evidence. Site = a location; sight = vision.

questions.prompt: In the sentence "They sat on the bank of the Cauvery and watched the sunset", the word 'bank' means:
options: a store of blood for hospitals
the land along the edge of a river
questions.explanation: 'Bank' is a homonym; here, with 'of the Cauvery', it means a river's edge.

questions.prompt: Which of the following pairs are HOMOPHONES (same sound, different spelling and meaning)?
questions.explanation: Knight and night sound the same but differ in spelling and meaning. 'Wind/wind' is a homograph (same spelling, different sound).

questions.prompt: "The classroom was a zoo when the teacher stepped out." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: The classroom is directly called a zoo, without 'like' or 'as', so it is a metaphor.

questions.prompt: "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: The same consonant sound /p/ is repeated at the beginning of nearby words: alliteration.

questions.prompt: "The old clock went tick-tock all through the night." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: 'Tick-tock' imitates the sound it describes: onomatopoeia.

questions.prompt: "O Death, where is thy sting?" Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: An absent person or an abstract idea (Death) is addressed directly: apostrophe.

questions.prompt: "Parting is such sweet sorrow." (Shakespeare) Identify the figure of speech in 'sweet sorrow'.
questions.explanation: Two opposite ideas, 'sweet' and 'sorrow', are placed side by side: oxymoron.

questions.prompt: "The pen is mightier than the sword." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: 'Pen' stands for writing/ideas and 'sword' for military force. An associated object names the thing: metonymy.

questions.prompt: The captain shouted, "All hands on deck!" The use of 'hands' for 'sailors' is an example of:
questions.explanation: A part (hands) stands for the whole (the sailors): synecdoche.

questions.prompt: "He is not a bad singer" (meaning he is quite a good singer). Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: Litotes is understatement that affirms something by denying its opposite.

questions.prompt: "Man proposes, God disposes." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: Contrasting ideas (proposes / disposes) are set in balanced phrases: antithesis.

questions.prompt: "The fire station burned down last night." This statement contains:
questions.explanation: The outcome is the opposite of what is expected (a fire station destroyed by fire): situational irony.

questions.prompt: "The soldier fought as brave as a lion." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: A comparison using 'as ... as' is a simile.

questions.prompt: "I am so hungry that I could eat an elephant." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: Deliberate, obvious exaggeration for effect is hyperbole.

questions.prompt: Which of the following lines contains a SIMILE?
options: My love is like a red, red rose.
The stars danced in the sky.
questions.explanation: Only Burns's line makes a comparison with 'like'. 'Life is a dream' and 'Time is money' are metaphors; 'stars danced' is personification.

questions.prompt: "The camera loves her; every photograph looks wonderful." Identify the figure of speech in 'The camera loves her'.
questions.explanation: A human feeling (love) is given to a non-living object (camera): personification.

questions.prompt: "His grandfather passed away last winter." The phrase 'passed away' is an example of:
questions.explanation: A mild expression used instead of a harsh one ('died') is a euphemism.

questions.prompt: "A bicycle cannot stand on its own because it is two-tired." Identify the figure of speech.
questions.explanation: 'Two-tired' plays on 'too tired' (two tyres): a pun is a play on words with similar sounds.

questions.prompt: "He spent a sleepless night before the examination." Identify the figure of speech in 'sleepless night'.
questions.explanation: It is the person, not the night, who is sleepless; the epithet is transferred from the person to the night.

questions.prompt: The repetition of similar VOWEL sounds in nearby words is called:
questions.explanation: Assonance repeats vowel sounds; alliteration repeats initial consonants; consonance repeats consonant sounds.

questions.prompt: "Can storied urn or animated bust / Back to its mansion call the fleeting breath?" (Gray) The question asked only for effect, expecting no answer, is called:
questions.explanation: A question asked for effect, not for an answer, is a rhetorical question (interrogation). The implied answer here is 'No'.

questions.prompt: "Every day, every hour, every minute, I think of my village." The repetition of 'every' at the start of successive phrases is:
questions.explanation: Repeating the same word at the beginning of successive phrases or clauses is anaphora.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb that correctly collocates: "The police are investigating who ___ the crime."
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'commit a crime'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct collocation: "There was ___ traffic on the highway during the festival."
questions.explanation: English uses 'heavy traffic' for a large volume of vehicles.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct collocation: "A good leader always ___ his promise."
questions.explanation: The natural collocation is 'keep a promise' (opposite: break a promise).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct collocation: "Murugan ___ a mistake in the last sum."
questions.explanation: We 'make a mistake' but 'do homework'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct collective noun: "A ___ of lions rested under the tree."
questions.explanation: A group of lions is a 'pride'. A herd is used for cattle or elephants, a pack for wolves, a flock for sheep or birds.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct collective noun: "A ___ of wolves howled in the forest."
questions.explanation: A group of wolves is a 'pack'. A swarm is used for bees, a school for fish.

questions.prompt: Add the correct prefix to form the opposite of 'legal':
questions.explanation: Words beginning with 'l' usually take the prefix il-: illegal, illogical, illiterate.

questions.prompt: Add the correct prefix to form the opposite of 'responsible':
questions.explanation: Words beginning with 'r' usually take ir-: irresponsible, irregular, irrelevant.

questions.prompt: Add the correct prefix to form the opposite of 'agree':
questions.explanation: The opposite of agree is formed with dis-: disagree.

questions.prompt: Add the correct prefix to 'patient' to mean 'not patient; easily annoyed':
questions.explanation: Words beginning with 'p' or 'm' often take im-. 'Inpatient' is a different word: a patient who stays in hospital.

questions.prompt: Add the correct suffix to the verb 'arrive' to form a noun: "We waited for the ___ of the train."
questions.explanation: Arrive + -al = arrival (like refuse -> refusal, approve -> approval).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct adjective formed from the noun 'courage':
questions.explanation: Courage + -ous keeps the 'e' to keep the 'g' soft: courageous.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb form of the noun 'strength':
questions.explanation: The suffix -en makes verbs from nouns and adjectives: strengthen, lengthen, sharpen.

questions.prompt: Choose the correctly formed adjective from the noun 'mischief':
questions.explanation: Mischief -> mischievous (four syllables, mis-chie-vous). 'Mischievious' is a common error.

questions.prompt: The word 'smog' is a blend of which two words?
questions.explanation: Smog = smoke + fog, a blend (portmanteau) word.

questions.prompt: The word 'motel' is a blend of which two words?
questions.explanation: Motel = motor + hotel: a roadside hotel for motorists.

questions.prompt: The word 'exam' is formed from 'examination' by which word-formation process?
questions.explanation: Shortening a longer word (examination -> exam, laboratory -> lab) is clipping.

questions.prompt: The word 'LASER' is an acronym of:
options: Light Activated by Sound and Electric Radiation
Long Amplified Signal of Electric Rays
Light Absorption by Stimulated Electron Rays
Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation

questions.prompt: What is the American English equivalent of the British English word 'lift' (in a building)?

questions.prompt: What is the American English equivalent of the British English word 'lorry'?
questions.explanation: British 'lorry' = American 'truck'.

questions.prompt: "The huge bungalow he inherited turned out to be a white elephant." The idiom 'a white elephant' means:

a valuable gift from a king
questions.explanation: A white elephant is something expensive to maintain but of little use.

questions.prompt: "The day India won its independence was a red-letter day for every citizen." A 'red-letter day' is:
questions.explanation: A red-letter day is a specially happy or significant day (festivals were once marked in red in calendars).

to avoid coming to the main point

questions.explanation: To let the cat out of the bag is to disclose a secret, usually by mistake.

questions.explanation: At the eleventh hour = at the latest possible moment before it is too late.

questions.prompt: "The landlord turned a deaf ear to the tenants' complaints." The idiom 'turn a deaf ear' means:
questions.explanation: To turn a deaf ear is to deliberately ignore a request or complaint.

questions.prompt: "Having broken the rules, the students had to face the music." The idiom 'face the music' means:
options: to accept the consequences of one's actions
questions.explanation: To face the music means to accept criticism or punishment for something one has done.

questions.prompt: "The news of his transfer came as a bolt from the blue." The idiom 'a bolt from the blue' means:
questions.explanation: A bolt from the blue is a sudden, unexpected event, like lightning from a clear sky.

questions.explanation: To add fuel to the fire is to make an angry or difficult situation worse.

questions.prompt: "Raju is in hot water for losing the office keys." The idiom 'in hot water' means:
questions.explanation: To be in hot water means to be in trouble or disgrace.

questions.prompt: "When the stranger offered to double her money, she smelt a rat." The idiom 'smell a rat' means:
options: to suspect that something is wrong
questions.explanation: To smell a rat means to suspect deception or trickery.

questions.prompt: "His father threw cold water on his plan to start a business." The idiom 'throw cold water on' means:
questions.explanation: To throw cold water on an idea is to discourage it or show no enthusiasm.

questions.prompt: "The poor widow took up tailoring to keep the wolf from the door." The idiom 'keep the wolf from the door' means:
options: to protect the house from wild animals
to earn just enough to avoid hunger and poverty
questions.explanation: To keep the wolf from the door is to have enough money to avoid starvation.

questions.prompt: "Take his promises with a pinch of salt." The idiom 'take with a pinch of salt' means:

questions.explanation: To take something with a pinch of salt is to be sceptical about it.

options: to undertake a dangerous task for the common good
questions.explanation: From the fable of the mice: to bell the cat is to take on a risky task that benefits everyone.

a person or problem that is difficult to deal with
questions.explanation: A hard nut to crack is someone or something difficult to understand or influence.

questions.explanation: To burn one's boats (or bridges) is to take an action that removes any chance of retreat.

questions.prompt: "Anita stayed home because she was feeling under the weather." The idiom 'under the weather' means:
questions.explanation: Under the weather = feeling slightly ill.

questions.explanation: Look into = examine or investigate.

questions.explanation: Make up for = compensate for something lost or missed.

questions.explanation: Turn up = arrive or appear, often unexpectedly or in small numbers.

questions.explanation: Put out = extinguish (a fire or light).

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Yesterday I ran ___ an old school friend at the bus stand."
questions.explanation: Run into = meet by chance. Run over = knock down with a vehicle; run down = criticise.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "The plane took ___ on time from Chennai airport."
